nodes.summary: Let $N$ be a list of natural numbers and $u$ an encoded right-hand side, that is, a word whose letters are nonterminals $i \in \mathbb{N}$ or terminals. The result is the list of all words obtained from $u$ by deleting some of the occurrences of nonterminals that belong to $N$ (possibly none, possibly all) and keeping every other letter in order; each choice of deleted occurrences contributes one entry of the list.
nodes.title: Deleting nonterminals from an encoded right-hand side

nodes.summary: For every encoded context-free grammar $g$, the grammar denoted by the encoded grammar obtained from $g$ by removing empty productions is equal to the grammar obtained from the grammar denoted by $g$ by eliminating empty productions: from each production, all productions obtained by deleting some occurrences of nullable nonterminals from its output, except those with empty output.
nodes.title: Computable removal of empty productions agrees with the classical one

nodes.summary: For an encoded context-free grammar $g$, the encoded grammar with the same start nonterminal whose productions are, for each production $A \to u$ of $g$, the productions $A \to v$ for every nonempty word $v$ obtained from $u$ by deleting some occurrences of nonterminals in the computed list of nullable nonterminals of $g$.
nodes.title: Removing empty productions from an encoded grammar

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar and consider the grammar of its productions without terminals. If a sentential form $\alpha$ that contains no terminal yields a word $w$ in that grammar, then $w$ is the empty word.
nodes.title: Terminal-free productions yield only the empty word

nodes.summary: For every encoded context-free grammar $g$, every production of the grammar denoted by the reduction of $g$ (empty productions removed, then unit productions removed) has a nonempty output, and that output is not a single nonterminal.
nodes.title: The reduced grammar has no empty and no unit productions

nodes.summary: For every encoded context-free grammar $g$, the language of the encoded grammar obtained from $g$ by removing empty productions consists of the nonempty words of the language of $g$.
nodes.title: Removing empty productions drops only the empty word

nodes.summary: For every encoded context-free grammar $g$, the language of the reduction of $g$ (empty productions removed, then unit productions removed) consists of the nonempty words of the language of $g$.
nodes.title: The reduced grammar generates the language minus the empty word

nodes.summary: For every encoded context-free grammar $g$, a production is a production of the grammar denoted by the encoded grammar obtained from $g$ by removing empty productions if and only if it is a production of the grammar obtained from the grammar denoted by $g$ by eliminating empty productions.
nodes.title: Productions of the computable removal of empty productions

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar. For every encoded word $u$ and every sentential form $\alpha$ of the grammar denoted by $g$, $\alpha$ is obtained from the decoding of $u$ by deleting some occurrences of nullable nonterminals of the grammar denoted by $g$ if and only if $\alpha$ is the decoding of a word obtained from $u$ by deleting some occurrences of nonterminals in the computed list of nullable…
nodes.title: Computed deletions agree with nullable deletions

nodes.summary: For every encoded context-free grammar $g$ and every natural number $A$, $A$ belongs to the computed list of nullable nonterminals of $g$ (the generating nonterminals of the productions of $g$ without terminals) if and only if $A$ is nullable in the grammar denoted by $g$, that is, $A$ derives the empty word.
nodes.title: The nullable nonterminals are computed

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar over terminals $T$ and let $r$ be a production with terminals in $T$ and nonterminals in $\mathbb{N}$. Then $r$ is a production of the grammar denoted by the encoded unit elimination of $g$ if and only if $r$ is a production of the grammar obtained from the grammar denoted by $g$ by eliminating unit productions.
nodes.title: Productions of the encoded unit elimination

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar and let $A$ and $B$ be natural numbers. Then $B$ belongs to the computed list of nonterminals reachable from $A$ by unit productions of $g$ if and only if there are $k \ge 0$ and nonterminals $A = C_0, C_1, \dots, C_k = B$ such that $C_{i-1} \to C_i$ is a production of the grammar denoted by $g$ for every $i$ with $1 \le i \le k$.
nodes.title: Unit reachability is computed

nodes.summary: For an encoded context-free grammar $g$, the encoded grammar with the same start nonterminal whose productions are the productions of $g$, in their order, whose right-hand sides contain no terminal.
nodes.title: Productions without terminals of an encoded grammar

nodes.summary: For an encoded context-free grammar $g$, the list obtained by duplicate removal from the list made of the start nonterminal of $g$ followed, for each production of $g$ in order, by its left-hand side and then the nonterminals of its right-hand side in order. It lists without repetitions the nonterminals that $g$ mentions.
nodes.title: Nonterminals of an encoded grammar

nodes.summary: For an encoded context-free grammar $g$, the list of generating nonterminals of the encoded grammar that has the start nonterminal of $g$ and, as productions, the productions of $g$ whose right-hand sides contain no terminal.
nodes.title: Computed nullable nonterminals of an encoded grammar

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a type of terminals with a primitive recursive encoding. The map sending an encoded context-free grammar $g$ over $T$ to its reduction, the encoded grammar obtained from $g$ by removing empty productions and then unit productions, is primitive recursive, where encoded grammars are encoded as pairs of a start nonterminal and a list of productions.
nodes.title: Reduction is primitive recursive

nodes.summary: For an encoded context-free grammar $g$, the encoded grammar obtained by first removing the empty productions of $g$ (encoded $\varepsilon$-elimination) and then removing the unit productions of the result (encoded unit elimination).
nodes.title: Reduction of an encoded grammar

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a context-free grammar over terminals $T$ and let $\alpha$ be a sentential form of $G$. If $\alpha$ yields the empty word in $G$, then no terminal symbol $a \in T$ occurs in $\alpha$.
nodes.title: A form yielding the empty word contains no terminal

nodes.summary: For every encoded context-free grammar $g$, the grammar denoted by the encoded unit elimination of $g$ is equal to the grammar obtained from the grammar denoted by $g$ by eliminating unit productions.
nodes.title: The encoded unit elimination denotes the unit-eliminated grammar

nodes.summary: For an encoded context-free grammar $g$, the encoded grammar with the start nonterminal of $g$ whose productions are listed as follows: for each nonterminal $A$ in the list of nonterminals of $g$, and for each production $B \to u$ of $g$ in order such that $B$ is in the computed list of nonterminals reachable from $A$ by unit productions and $u$ is not a single nonterminal, the production $A \to u$.
nodes.title: Unit elimination for encoded grammars

nodes.summary: For an encoded context-free grammar $g$ and a natural number $A$, let $n$ be the number of distinct nonterminals mentioned in $g$ (the start, the left-hand sides, and the nonterminals on right-hand sides). The list is obtained from the empty list by applying one round of unit reachability from $A$ exactly $n + 1$ times.
nodes.title: Nonterminals reachable by unit productions in an encoded grammar

nodes.summary: For an encoded context-free grammar $g$, a natural number $A$ and a list $S$ of natural numbers, the list consisting of $A$ followed, for each production of $g$ in order whose left-hand side lies in $S$ and whose right-hand side is a single nonterminal $B$, by that nonterminal $B$.
nodes.title: One round of unit reachability

nodes.summary: For an encoded right-hand side $u$, a list whose entries are nonterminals $i \in \mathbb{N}$ or terminals, the optional value is $B$ when $u$ consists of the single nonterminal $B$, and there is no value otherwise.
nodes.title: Target of a unit right-hand side

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar and $\alpha$ a sentential form of the grammar $g$ denotes. If $\alpha$ yields the empty word in that grammar, then $\alpha$ also yields the empty word in the grammar denoted by the encoded grammar consisting of the productions of $g$ that contain no terminal.
nodes.title: Yields of the empty word need only terminal-free productions

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar, $\alpha$ a sentential form and $w$ a word. If $\alpha$ yields $w$ in the grammar denoted by the encoded grammar consisting of the productions of $g$ that contain no terminal, then $\alpha$ yields $w$ in the grammar $g$ denotes.
nodes.title: Yields in the terminal-free subgrammar are yields of the grammar
Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
